prompt: Employers should give their staff at least four-weeks’ holiday a year to help employees get better at their jobs. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Some people argue that employers should provide their workers with at least four weeks of annual leave because this can improve job performance. I strongly agree with this view, as sufficient holiday time protects employees’ health, increases productivity, and creates a more motivated workforce.

To begin with, regular holidays allow employees to recover from the physical and mental pressure of work. In many modern jobs, people face long hours, tight deadlines, and constant communication through technology. Without enough time away from these demands, workers may become exhausted, stressed, and less able to concentrate. For example, an accountant who works continuously during busy financial periods may start making careless mistakes if they never have proper rest. Therefore, a reasonable amount of annual leave can help employees return to work with clearer minds and better focus.

Moreover, giving staff at least four weeks’ holiday can benefit employers as well as employees. Rested workers are often more creative, efficient, and loyal to their organisations. When employees feel that their company values their well-being, they are more likely to work hard and remain committed in the long term. In contrast, businesses that offer very little holiday may experience higher staff turnover, low morale, and reduced productivity. For instance, companies with generous leave policies often attract skilled applicants because they are seen as supportive and professional workplaces.

In conclusion, I fully agree that employees should receive a minimum of four weeks’ holiday each year. Far from being a waste of company time, adequate leave helps workers maintain their health, improve their performance, and develop stronger loyalty to their employers. For this reason, annual holidays should be regarded as an investment in workplace success.
